newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Oct 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Oct 28.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on Oct. 28:

WASHINGTON - Reform Party candidate Ross Perot insisted he is in the race to stay, but said that if the choice was limited to President Bill Clinton and Republican challenger Bob Dole, every American would pick Dole.
WASHINGTON - The 1996 presidential election is in part a referendum on whether President Bill Clinton has fought his way back to being an advocate for the middle class.
WASHINGTON - The Washington Redskins overpowered the Indianapolis Colts, 31-16, to improve to 7-1 their led in the National Football Conference's Eastern Division.

EVELETH, MINNESOTA - Lois Jenson and 20 other women miners at the taconite mine here filed a class-action lawsuit in 1988 against pervasive sexual harassment on the job, only to find that they would encounter a backlash of anger and retaliation from their co-workers.
LONDON - Ireland's "Father Ted" sitcom is all the rage in Britain, France, Iceland, New Zealand and Scandanavia, to name a few places.
WASHINGTON - The Clinton administration's strategy to pull U.S. peacekeeping troops out of Bosnia after one year has fallen apart.
